guidance.title: Match an Australian seller identifier to its scheme
guidance.summary:
When the seller address identifies Australia, the legal identifier needs to be an
ABN carried under the ABN scheme. A syntactically valid identifier from another
scheme does not become an ABN merely because it is placed in the seller record.
commonCauses: A New Zealand party template was reused for an Australian seller.
The identifier value was changed without changing its scheme.
Country-specific party data was mapped after a generic identifier block had already been produced.
guidance.fix:
Read the seller country and legal registration data from the same verified party
record. For an Australian seller, emit the verified ABN with scheme `0151`, then
validate the complete document again. The fixture values are official published
examples whose provenance and registry-check limits are documented in
`packages/fixtures/parties.md`; do not use them for a live transaction.

guidance.title: Label a New Zealand seller's NZBN correctly
guidance.summary:
For a seller located in New Zealand, the legal identifier and its scheme must
describe an NZBN consistently. The validator uses the country, identifier value,
and scheme together rather than treating the scheme as optional metadata.
commonCauses: A local company-number scheme was used where the interoperable NZBN scheme was needed.
The NZBN value was supplied but a default scheme remained on the XML element.
Seller country and registration fields came from different source records.
guidance.fix:
Confirm the seller's NZBN in the authoritative party data and carry it under
scheme `0088`. Revalidate the complete document after changing the scheme. The
fixture's NZBN is an official published example with provenance and live-use
limits recorded in `packages/fixtures/parties.md`.

guidance.title: Give the buyer a routing reference
guidance.summary:
The document needs at least one buyer-facing reference that can connect it to the
buyer's process. A buyer reference can provide that routing key when there is no
purchase order reference.
commonCauses: A non-order invoice was generated with the order block omitted and no alternative buyer reference.
A reference exists in the source system but was mapped only into free text.
Empty reference values were removed during XML cleanup.
guidance.fix:
Use a real reference supplied or agreed by the buyer. Put it in either the buyer
reference or purchase order reference location as appropriate; do not invent an
order number merely to pass validation. Revalidate the whole document.

guidance.title: Include the destination account for a credit transfer
guidance.summary:
Selecting credit transfer as the payment method is not enough to tell the payer
where funds should go. The payment block also needs the payee account identifier
used for that transfer.
commonCauses: Payment method and bank details were mapped by separate integrations.
Account data was suppressed while the credit-transfer code remained.
A payment block was copied from a non-bank payment flow.
guidance.fix:
If credit transfer is the intended method, add the payee's verified account
identifier in the financial account block. Otherwise select the payment method
that describes the real arrangement. Never fabricate account details, and
revalidate the complete document.

guidance.title: Keep line tax classification under GST
guidance.summary:
An A-NZ line tax classification is interpreted within the GST tax scheme. A
category and percentage attached to a different scheme do not form the expected
line GST classification.
commonCauses: A European invoice template supplied `VAT` as a global default.
Tax scheme and category were populated from different tax engines.
A label intended for display was reused as the scheme code.
guidance.fix:
Map the line's tax decision as one coherent set: category, rate where applicable,
and scheme. Use `GST` only when that reflects the source transaction and relevant
authoritative requirements; this validation result is not tax advice. Revalidate
the entire document because the category must also agree with its tax breakdown.

guidance.title: Reconcile quantity, price, and line net amount
guidance.summary:
The line's stated net amount needs to reconcile its priced quantity and any
line-level adjustments. Start with quantity multiplied by the unit price after
allowing for a price base quantity, add line charges, and subtract line
allowances. Changing document totals to match a wrong line amount does not repair
the line calculation.
commonCauses: A unit price was rounded or converted independently from the line total.
The source quantity changed after the total was calculated.
A price base quantity was ignored by the mapping.
A line allowance or charge was included in the XML but omitted from the line-net calculation.
guidance.fix:
Recalculate from the authoritative line inputs, keeping currency precision and
the price base quantity consistent. Include each line charge as an addition and
each line allowance as a subtraction exactly once. This minimal fixture has no
line adjustments, so two units at `50.00` produce the stated `100.00` line net
amount. Revalidate all totals after the correction.

guidance.title: Use a supported media type for embedded evidence
guidance.summary:
The A-NZ profile narrows the media types accepted for an embedded supporting
document. The declared media type must describe both an allowed format and the
bytes that were actually encoded.
commonCauses: An internal XML export was attached directly.
A filename extension was changed without converting the content.
A broader UBL media-type list was used instead of the A-NZ subset.
guidance.fix:
Convert the supporting material to a supported format, then update its filename,
media type, and base64 payload together. Do not merely relabel unchanged bytes.
The corrected fixture uses a tiny synthetic CSV payload. Revalidate the complete
document and test that the decoded attachment opens as declared.

guidance.title: State what kind of billing document this is
guidance.summary:
The document root distinguishes invoice XML from credit-note XML, but the
business document also needs its functional type code in the matching type-code
element.
commonCauses: The type code was treated as redundant with the XML root.
A source document type had no mapping to the PINT code list.
An empty code was removed by serialization.
guidance.fix:
Choose the code that accurately represents the business document and place it in
the type-code element for that document root. The fixture is an ordinary invoice,
so it uses `380`. Do not copy this value to a credit note without mapping its real
type. Revalidate the complete document.

guidance.title: Include the seller's registered name
guidance.summary:
A seller legal identifier does not substitute for the seller name. The legal
entity block needs the name by which the seller is identified in the transaction.
commonCauses: Only identifier fields were selected from the supplier master record.
A trading name was mapped elsewhere while the legal name was left empty.
Whitespace-only names were removed during serialization.
guidance.fix:
Populate the seller registration name from verified party data and keep the
identifier as a separate field. Confirm that the chosen name is appropriate for
the transaction; validation cannot establish legal identity. Revalidate the
complete document.

guidance.title: Give every line quantity a unit
guidance.summary:
A numeric line quantity is ambiguous without a unit of measure. The unit belongs
on the quantity element as a code, not in the item description.
commonCauses: The source system stores quantity but leaves its unit implicit.
A display label such as “each” was not mapped to a unit code.
The serializer emitted the quantity text but dropped its attribute.
guidance.fix:
Map the source unit to the appropriate supported code. `EA` is correct only for
the synthetic fixture's count of individual items; choose the unit that describes
the actual line. Recalculate any unit-dependent prices and revalidate the whole
document.

guidance.title: Put document-period dates in chronological order
guidance.summary:
When both boundaries of the document period are present, the end cannot precede
the start. This check concerns ordering; it does not decide which service dates
the transaction should use.
commonCauses: Start and end fields were swapped during mapping.
A date range crossed a month boundary and the month was copied incorrectly.
Locale-specific input was parsed with the wrong day and month order.
guidance.fix:
Return to the source period, correct the mapped dates, and serialize them as ISO
dates. Do not reverse values automatically without confirming their meaning. The
fixture is corrected to end after it starts, then the complete document is
revalidated.

guidance.title: Explain a document-level allowance
guidance.summary:
A document-level reduction needs a reason that a receiver can understand or
process. Its amount and percentage describe the calculation, not why the
allowance exists.
commonCauses: The source discount has an amount but no mapped reason.
A reason code was stored in an internal field and omitted from the export.
Calculation fields were copied without their business context.
guidance.fix:
Provide the genuine allowance reason as text or, where suitable, a supported
reason code. Do not invent a commercial reason. The synthetic fixture adds text;
after any correction, recheck the allowance arithmetic, tax category, and
document totals.

guidance.title: Keep one project reference
guidance.summary:
A billing document has one project-reference slot in the semantic model. In a
credit note, that reference is represented through a specially typed additional
document reference; adding a second one creates another project reference rather
than extra description for the first.
commonCauses: Several project codes from a source record were exported independently.
An existing reference was appended instead of replaced during an update.
A generic supporting-document loop emitted more than one project-typed entry.
guidance.fix:
Select the single project that the billing document actually concerns. If other
references are needed, map them only to their correct business terms rather than
labelling them as projects. The corrected synthetic credit note removes the
duplicate and is revalidated in full.

guidance.title: Map the payment method to a supported code
guidance.summary:
The payment means value is a code, not a free internal payment-method identifier.
It must come from the supported external list and describe the actual arrangement.
commonCauses: An ERP's internal numeric payment code was copied directly.
A display label was converted to an arbitrary number.
Code-list validation was omitted from the outbound mapping.
guidance.fix:
Map the source payment method to the matching supported code. The synthetic
fixture uses `10` for a cash scenario; choose a different code when the real
payment method differs. Add any details required by that method and revalidate
the complete document.

guidance.title: Rebuild totals from the lines
guidance.summary:
The document's line-net total is a roll-up of the individual line net amounts.
Compensating other totals to agree with an incorrect roll-up may hide additional
errors, but it does not make the roll-up correct.
commonCauses: A deleted or filtered line remained in a cached header total.
Header totals and lines were rounded or converted in separate operations.
A manual total override bypassed recalculation.
guidance.fix:
Recompute the line-net total from the final serialized lines, then recalculate the
dependent tax-exclusive, tax-inclusive, and payable values from their own source
terms. The synthetic fixture has one `100.00` line and is corrected consistently.
Revalidate the complete totals chain.
